beats.gist: At the Lisbon quay Joaquim reads the wind, says it will be an upwind crossing to Almada under sail and oars, and notes his passenger has not said why she is going.
As the player turns through the wind, Joaquim gives a short instruction to bring the bow across and sheet in on the new side.
On a calm leg the passenger asks why they keep zigzagging; Joaquim explains that a boat cannot sail straight into the wind, and points out the other craft that work the same river.

beats.concept: Getting out of irons: arribar, folgar then caçar
beats.gist: The boat stalls head to wind and Joaquim gives a short instruction to bear away and let the sail fill again.

Once the boat is moving again, the passenger asks why he stays in this work; Joaquim answers that the river is the road between the two banks and boats are the fastest way across, and she finally says why she is going to Almada.

beats.concept: Approach and dock (acostar), controlling speed to come alongside
beats.gist: Joaquim brings the catraio alongside at Almada and says a quiet line about the people he carries; the passenger pays and steps ashore.

Optional card separating fact from fiction: Joaquim and the passenger are invented, while the catraio, its passenger trade between the banks, and the river traffic that lasted until the mid-20th century and the 1966 bridge are documented.
